questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the relation between the distance between two objects (d) and the gravitational force (F) produced between them?
options: F is directly proportional to d squared
F is inversely proportional to d squared
F is inversely proportional to d
F is directly proportional to d
questions.explanation: Gravitational force decreases when distance increases. It follows F proportional to 1/d^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the change in gravitational force between two objects when their masses are doubled?
options: The force is reduced two times
The force is decreased four times
questions.explanation: Gravitational force depends on both masses. If both masses double, the force becomes four times.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If the gravitational force between two objects on Earth is 60 N, what is the gravitational force between those two objects on the Moon?
questions.explanation: The same two objects have the same masses and distance. So their mutual gravitational force remains 60 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement is correct?
options: The value of acceleration due to gravity increases as we go deeper from Earth's surface
The value of g is less at the poles than at the equator
The value of acceleration due to gravity decreases as height above Earth's surface increases
The value of g is highest at the highest place on Earth
questions.explanation: As height from Earth's surface increases, g decreases. So acceleration due to gravity becomes smaller.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: At which place do you weigh the most?
questions.explanation: Weight is greater where g is greater. Low altitude places are nearer to Earth's centre, so weight is more there.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: The radius of Earth is 6371 km and an object weighs 800 N on Earth. What is its weight at a height of 6371 km from Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: At height equal to Earth's radius, distance from centre becomes double. So weight becomes one-fourth of 800 N, which is 200 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If the mass and radius of a celestial body are twice those of Earth, what is the value of acceleration due to gravity there?
questions.explanation: g depends on mass divided by radius squared. Twice mass and twice radius gives half of Earth's g.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What will be the weight of a man on the Moon if his weight on Earth is 750 N? (g on Moon = 1.63 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: Weight on Moon = Earth weight x Moon g / Earth g. So 750 x 1.63 / 9.8 = 124.74 N.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Planet B has twice the mass and half the radius of planet A. Planet C has half the mass and twice the radius of planet A. Which order of weights is correct?
questions.explanation: Planet B has larger mass and smaller radius, so its g is greatest. Planet C has smaller mass and larger radius, so its g is least.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which conclusion is correct while observing a freely falling object every second?
questions.explanation: In free fall, acceleration is constant. So velocity increases by equal amount every second.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is gravity?
options: The force that acts only inside water
The force with which Earth attracts objects towards its centre
The speed of a moving object
questions.explanation: Gravity is Earth's pulling force. It pulls objects toward the centre of Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is gravitational force?
options: Force that exists only on Earth
Mutual force of attraction between any two bodies having mass
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is attraction between any two bodies with mass. It is not only on Earth.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the SI unit of force used for weight?
questions.explanation: Weight is a force. The SI unit of force is newton.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the value of the universal gravitational constant G given in the chapter?
questions.explanation: G is the universal gravitational constant. Its value is 6.67 x 10^-11 Nm^2/kg^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula represents Newton's universal law of gravitation?
questions.explanation: Newton's law says force depends on two masses and distance squared. So the formula is F = Gm1m2/d^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is acceleration due to gravity?
options: Acceleration produced in a body due to gravity
questions.explanation: Acceleration due to gravity is acceleration caused by gravity. It is written as g.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity at Earth's surface used in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The value of g on Earth's surface is 9.8 m/s^2. This value is used in most calculations.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is free fall?
options: Motion of a body under the effect of gravity only
Motion of a body pushed by wind only
Motion of a body in water only
questions.explanation: Free fall means falling under gravity only. No other force is considered.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is mass?
options: Force of gravity on a body
Amount of matter in a body
questions.explanation: Mass means amount of matter in a body. It does not change from place to place.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is weight?
options: Measure of gravitational force acting on a body
questions.explanation: Weight is the force of gravity on a body. It changes when g changes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is acceleration due to gravity not the same everywhere on Earth?
options: Earth's radius and position from the centre vary
questions.explanation: g depends on distance from Earth's centre. So it changes with height and latitude.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does weight decrease when a person climbs Mount Everest?
options: g decreases with height above Earth's surface
questions.explanation: Weight = mass x g. On high mountains, g is less, so weight decreases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is a parachute not useful for landing safely on the Moon?
options: There is no atmosphere for air resistance
questions.explanation: A parachute needs air resistance to slow down. The Moon has no atmosphere, so it cannot work well there.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why do a coin and feather reach together in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: In vacuum, there is no air resistance. So a coin and feather fall with the same acceleration.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does folded paper fall faster than a flat sheet in air?
options: Gravity acts only on folded paper
questions.explanation: Folded paper has less air resistance than flat paper. So it falls faster in air.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which equation of motion is used for a freely falling body starting from rest?
questions.explanation: For free fall from rest, initial velocity is zero. So the equation becomes s = 1/2 gt^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: How is weight related to mass?
questions.explanation: Weight is mass multiplied by g. So the formula is W = mg.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is it difficult to lift a big stone on Earth?
options: Earth's gravity gives it a large weight
Air pushes it downward more than gravity
questions.explanation: A big stone has large mass. Earth's gravity gives it large weight, so lifting is difficult.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to the acceleration due to gravity when Earth's radius decreases but mass remains the same?
questions.explanation: g = GM/R^2. If radius decreases and mass is same, g increases.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which factor does not change the mass of an object?
options: Moving it from Earth to Moon
questions.explanation: Mass depends on amount of matter. Moving from Earth to Moon does not change the matter.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does weight vary from place to place?
options: Because mass always varies with place
Because acceleration due to gravity varies
questions.explanation: Weight depends on g. Since g changes from place to place, weight also changes.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: When is gravitational force equal to the gravitational constant G?
options: When objects are on the Moon only
When both masses are 1 kg and distance between centres is 1 m
questions.explanation: F becomes equal to G when both masses are 1 kg and distance is 1 m. This comes from F = Gm1m2/d^2.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which statement about g at poles and equator matches the chapter idea?
options: g is zero at the poles
g is greater at the equator than at the poles
g is the same everywhere regardless of radius
g is greater at the poles than at the equator
questions.explanation: Earth is slightly flattened at the poles. The polar radius is smaller, so g is greater there.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which pair correctly compares mass and weight?
options: Mass is measured in N; weight is measured in kg
Mass is measured in kg; weight is measured in N
Both are measured only in second
questions.explanation: Mass is measured in kilogram. Weight is a force, so it is measured in newton.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to gravitational force if the distance between two objects becomes half?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is inversely proportional to distance squared. Half distance makes force four times.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What happens to gravitational force if only one mass is doubled?
questions.explanation: Force is directly proportional to mass. If one mass doubles, force also doubles.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which is an example of free fall?
options: A stone falling in vacuum under gravity
A car moving on a road
A boat floating in a river
questions.explanation: Free fall means only gravity acts on the body. A stone falling in vacuum is a good example.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does a person feel an eerie sensation while moving downward in a Rote Ping?
options: Apparent weight decreases during downward acceleration
questions.explanation: While moving downward, support force becomes less. So the person feels lighter for a moment.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which quantity remains constant for a body taken from Earth to Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass stays the same everywhere. Weight changes because g is different on Earth and Moon.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: What is the main cause of variation in gravitational force with distance?
options: Force follows inverse square relation with distance
questions.explanation: Gravitational force follows inverse square law. So changing distance changes force strongly.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A body is taken to a planet where g is twice Earth's g. What happens to its weight?
options: It becomes half while mass doubles
It becomes twice while mass remains the same
questions.explanation: Weight = mg. If g becomes twice, weight also becomes twice but mass remains same.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why does Jupiter not have 319 times Earth's g although its mass is about 319 times Earth's mass?
options: Its mass has no effect on g
Its much larger radius reduces g according to GM/R^2
questions.explanation: Jupiter has very large mass, but it also has very large radius. Large radius reduces the value of g.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If two bodies are dropped from the same height in polar and equatorial regions, which falls faster and why?
options: The polar one, because g is greater there
The equatorial one, because g is zero at poles
The polar one, because mass decreases
questions.explanation: g is greater at the poles. So a body falls faster in the polar region.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A person says mass and weight are the same because both are measured on balances. What is the correct response?
options: They are exactly the same quantity
They differ: mass is matter, weight is gravitational force
Mass is measured in newton only
questions.explanation: Mass is amount of matter. Weight is gravitational force, so they are different.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If Earth were squeezed to a smaller radius without changing mass, what would happen to g?
options: It would decrease because mass is same
It would increase because radius is in the denominator squared
It would be unrelated to radius
questions.explanation: g = GM/R^2. If Earth radius becomes smaller, g becomes greater.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: A feather and a marble fall together only in a vacuum. Which two ideas are needed to explain this?
options: Equal gravitational acceleration and absence of air resistance
No gravity and high air resistance
Different g and same air resistance
questions.explanation: Vacuum removes air resistance. Then both feather and marble fall with the same acceleration.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which change produces the greatest gravitational force?
options: Halving one mass and doubling distance
Keeping masses small and increasing distance
Doubling both masses and halving the distance
questions.explanation: Greater masses increase gravitational force. Smaller distance also increases gravitational force.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: If a body is in free fall, which force is considered to be acting on it?
questions.explanation: In free fall, only gravity acts on the body. Other forces are not considered.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Why is weightlessness not the same as absence of gravity?
options: It is a condition of apparent weight becoming zero during free fall
It means Earth has no attraction
It occurs only when g is always zero
questions.explanation: Weightlessness means apparent weight becomes zero. Gravity may still be acting.

questions.subject: science
questions.question: Which formula explains why g decreases at high altitude?
questions.explanation: At height h, distance from Earth's centre is R+h. So g is given by GM/(R+h)^2.
